texts.facts: Vide this judgment, I propose to dispose off the appeal filed u/S 70 of The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006("FSS Act" in short). Vide the present appeal, the order dated 19.11.2019 has been challenged vide which Ld.Adjudicating Officer/ADM(East) ("AO" in short) imposed a penalty of Rs.30,000/ each on all the appellants. 2. The present appeal has been filed on 06.11.2020 alongwith an application for condonation of delay. In the application for condonation of delay, it has been submitted that the appeal could not be filed within limitation period due to misconception that the order has to be passed by the court. It has been submitted that the appellants on 20.02.2020 and 21.02.2020 received notice regarding deposition of Demand Draft of penalty, issued by the respondent and after receiving the above notices, the appellants contacted their previous counsel and one month delay was caused by the previous counsel for his personal reason and thereafter, period of lock down started. Thus, the appeal could not be filed within limitation period. Ld. Counsel for the appellants submitted that there was no deliberate attempt on the part of the appellants to cause the delay. 3. Per contra, Ld.Chief PP for respondent has submitted that there is no jurisdiction with the present court to condone the delay.
texts.arguments: Provided, however, that the Appellate Tribunal may allow a maximum of another 30 days to entertain an appeal if it is satisfied that there was sufficient cause for not filing the appeal within first 30 days." Another contention by the Ld.Counsel for the appellants is that there was mis conception that appeal can be filed only after the direction of the court, is also not tenable.
